notes: IMD6900RobinhoodLaunch is the one deployed contract, on Robinhood Chain (chain id 4663). Constructor (owner_, poolManager_, imdstr_, timelock_): 0x35da9c0303507ddf708e87f2568eddf12c47a059 is the owner, the team wallet the brief states (written as the static address), which later calls launch() to create the IMD6900 coin at a mined 0x6900... address, open the locked coin-only pool and make the opening buy in one transaction; 0x8366a39CC670B4001A1121B8F6A443A643e40951 is Uniswap v4's PoolManager on Robinhood Chain (stored, not called at deploy); 0x0000198C940D8cD70Cb9ACeC5E3af8216ac57d2F is Robinhood's IMDSTR, the old token whose holders claim the new coin 1:1; 0x16D3f65B708883DF042d98E1C7a49B32A33E2A14 is the Robinhood timelock, which owns the hook and the perps engine, recovers ETH, releases the excess, sells the held coins (sellHeld), ends the claims early (endClaims), lowers the pool fee (lowerFee, lower only, refused while perps positions are open) and alone sets the fee split and landing addresses (setPayees, setPerpFeeTo, setCoinFeeTo, setImdBurn, setImdPool). The constructor creates IMD6900LockedPool (static 4.44% fee, POOL_FEE 44_400) and nothing else: no salt mining, no external call, about 6.9M gas from any deployer, so it deploys the same on a fresh chain and fits one transaction. After the deploy, anyone calls createHook(salt) once with a salt mined off-chain against the pool's address (script/launch.sh hook) so IMD6900LockedPool creates IMD6900Hook with CREATE2 at an address carrying exactly the hook's permission flags; the team does this, not the deployment. The perps (PerpEngine, PerpVault) are not deployed here: IMD6900LockedPool.createPerps creates them right after launch() from the code bound by ENGINE_CODE_HASH / VAULT_CODE_HASH. Fee split defaults are fixed in the code: 90% to the pot bridge, 10% $IMD bought for the canonical Robinhood burn executor 0x4D6537ec564aFf82eABb1Ce5f355E817cBEA1e07. No ETH is sent at deploy and no initialization call is needed.
